confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors are based on a few web searches that returned aggregated, crowd-sourced cost-of-living figures. Expatica, using Numbeo data from June 2026, gives a cappuccino at about $5.04, a domestic draught beer at $8, an inexpensive meal at $25 and a three-course meal for two at $110. MyLifeElsewhere gives about $5.79 for a cappuccino, $8 for a pint and $22 for an inexpensive meal. The figures used are blended midpoints. The cocktail and wine anchors rest on weaker evidence. Cities Insider's 2026 guide lists standard cocktails at $15–18 and puts wine by the glass anywhere from $12–16 to $14–22. Expatistan has about $18 for a cocktail, but from very few data points. Wine is the least certain drink anchor. Prices in Boston vary a lot by neighbourhood, with Downtown and Seaport at the high end. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge only, adjusted for July as peak summer season. No live listings or booking pages were checked. Boston has very few registered hostels and its hotel rates are high, so the accommodation anchors are uncertain and could vary by ±25% or more. For the FX figure, the search results attributed 0.6720 USD per AUD on 2026-11-18 to the RBA 4.00 pm fixing. I took that from search-result summaries, including a third-party aggregator, and did not open the RBA page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Boston is treated as a high-cost US East Coast city. Its drink prices are slightly below Manhattan's, roughly an $8.25 pint versus $10.50. Accommodation in July is benchmarked against peak-season pricing in high-cost US cities such as New York, San Francisco and Washington DC.
